acknowledgements.reason: Approved for the 26.2 WasmGC target: T7 evidence D:/gaius-next/v040/m1/out7/train-T7/smoke/acc-26.2-wasm-gl-sr/console.log reports GaiusChunkSections as unsupported in terrain pipelines. Registering the block in GlProgram.uniformsByName before vanilla's active-block scan prevents that warning and preserves BrowserOpenGL's last uniform-buffer binding used by ensureTerrainUbo. The patch is WasmGC-only; frozen JavaScript output remains unchanged.

The light kernel patches now also apply to the 1.21.11 wasmgc target (rewrites of ThreadedLevelLightEngine.lightChunk/checkBlock plus the kernel hooks, routed through LightVersionOps for the getLightBlock/ChunkPos naming). javap shows the 1.21.11 and 26.2 light engines differ only in lambda numbering and that method name; the patched first-light route matches vanilla on 63,897,600 nibbles (2 seeds x 6 modes incl. kernel off, simd, baseline, declines and failure fallback) and the column goldens match on 270/270 cases. The frozen js target keeps vanilla lighting (NOT_APPLICABLE for js).

Approved by the repository owner (2026-10-09). The fast-ring rewrite of the generateRingPositions search lambda leaves the wasmgc lock: it returned each concentric-ring start chunk without vanilla's biome search and moved 699 of 768 stronghold positions (6 seeds, structure-rings-parity.mjs against the old patch). WebAssembly GC applies patchChunkGeneratorStructureStateBrowserLazyRings instead: the lazy ring positions keep vanilla's loop, RNG draws and biome search and only defer each search; JVM parity 768/768 positions and 9558/9558 contains() answers identical to vanilla on 6 seeds x 3 profiles (structure-rings-parity.mjs --target wasmgc).

Owner approval (TypeThe0ry, 2026-10-11): keep patchNoiseChunkBrowserSynchronous JavaScript-only. It rewrites the NoiseChunk counters from long to int for the JavaScript build while its CacheOnce/context companions stay JavaScript-only, so on WebAssembly GC NoiseChunk$CacheOnce.fillArray read an int field as long and TeaVM emitted an invalid module (train T6: 26.2 and 1.21.11 clients failed WebAssembly.validate, 'i64.add expected type i64, found struct.get of type i32'). The wasm build keeps vanilla's NoiseChunk; the patch is a JavaScript coroutine/perf rewrite, not a cooperation point.

Owner approval (TypeThe0ry, 2026-10-12): WasmGC-only cooperative waits in BlockableEventLoop.managedBlock (6e67dfa4 + 284ab526 from the parity6 branch). Vanilla managedBlock keeps running tasks while pollTask() returns true and never reaches waitForTasks(), so worldgen worker replies, MessagePort work and timers starved and the radius-3 PLAYER_SPAWN preparation hung the server handshake. The WasmGC rewrite yields after a 2 ms busy slice or an empty poll. Evidence: DEBUG 26.3 server capture TICK_WORKER_CAPTURE ticks=40, waitForEntities completes, no handshake timeout; non-DEBUG world entry 5/5 (median 25.9 s vs T7 28.6 s). JavaScript target unchanged (strict compare js: 0 differences).

Owner approval (TypeThe0ry, 2026-10-12): WasmGC keeps vanilla's PLAYER_SPAWN preparation radius 3 and no longer injects the JavaScript-only entity gate (7269e685 from the parity6 branch); the JavaScript build keeps its radius-1 workaround. Needed for vanilla parity of the spawn area; made safe by the cooperative managedBlock waits. Evidence: DEBUG 26.3 capture ticks=40 with waitForEntities completing; non-DEBUG world entry 5/5 on T7 acceptance-26.3. JavaScript target unchanged.
